sources.summary: Loss of maternal UBE3A activity in neurons is central to Angelman syndrome. Developmental delay, severe speech impairment, ataxia and seizures are characteristic. Large deletions may involve additional genes.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.summary: Pathogenic CDKL5 variants cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with early seizures and severe developmental impairment. CDKL5 is on the X chromosome.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.summary: CDKL5 deficiency involves loss of function. Neurological features include epilepsy, developmental impairment and cortical visual impairment.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.summary: STXBP1 loss of function impairs neurotransmitter release. Developmental impairment, epilepsy and movement abnormalities occur. Inheritance is autosomal dominant, usually de novo.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.source: Lipman et al.: Clinical and genetic characterization of CACNA1A-related disease
sources.summary: A clinical cohort describes heterogeneous CACNA1A-related neurological phenotypes. Gene-level association does not establish the functional direction of an individual variant.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.source: From genotype to phenotype: CACNA1A variants
sources.summary: CACNA1A disorders include gain- and loss-of-function mechanisms, with hemiplegic migraine, episodic ataxia and developmental epileptic phenotypes. Variant-specific direction is required.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.source: Huang et al.: Topoisomerase inhibitors unsilence the dormant allele of Ube3a in neurons
sources.summary: Topotecan restored paternal Ube3a expression in neuronal models by reducing an antisense transcript. This is experimental unsilencing evidence, not clinical efficacy.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success
sources.excerpt: These results indicate that topotecan unsilences Ube3a in cis by reducing transcription of an imprinted antisense RNA.

sources.source: Meng et al.: Towards a therapy for Angelman syndrome by targeting a long non-coding RNA
sources.summary: UBE3A-ATS antisense perturbations restored paternal UBE3A in mouse models. The authors compared selective antisense effects with topotecan effects on long-gene transcription; phenotypic rescue was incomplete.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.source: King et al.: Topoisomerases facilitate transcription of long genes linked to autism
sources.summary: Topotecan reduced transcription of long neuronal genes in mouse and human models. This broad transcriptional effect is a spillover concern when probing UBE3A unsilencing.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.source: Fink et al.: Disrupted neuronal maturation in Angelman syndrome-derived induced pluripotent stem cells
sources.summary: Angelman-derived neuronal models showed electrophysiological maturation deficits; topotecan increased synaptic-event frequency in this in-vitro setting.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.source: Ube3a unsilencer for the potential treatment of Angelman syndrome
sources.summary: (S)-PHA533533 unsilenced paternal Ube3a in models. The effect was independent of its known CDK2/CDK5 targets and TOP1 inhibition. It is a research compound, not an approved repurposed drug.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.summary: Oncology labeling warns of severe myelosuppression and identifies renal impairment as relevant to exposure. It supplies no validated organ-burden number for Angelman research.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.source: Knight et al.: Ganaxolone phase 3 trial in CDKL5 deficiency disorder
sources.summary: A randomized trial assessed ganaxolone for seizures in CDKL5 deficiency disorder. Symptom-directed clinical evidence does not show restoration of the causal CDKL5 deficit.
sources.evidence_level: source-specific; not a probability of treatment success

sources.source: Chamberlain et al.: iPSC models of Angelman and Prader-Willi imprinting disorders
sources.summary: The study generated iPSC models of Angelman and Prader-Willi syndromes and studied maintenance of genomic imprinting. It supplies a shared experimental approach, not evidence for a shared treatment.

sources.summary: Prader-Willi syndrome involves loss of expression of paternal chromosome-15 genes, including the SNORD116 region. It is a complex imprinting disorder, not simply UBE3A loss of function.

diseases.name: Angelman syndrome
diseases.mechanism: Loss of maternal neuronal UBE3A; paternal allele is normally silenced. Demo scope: UBE3A deficiency, not all deletion biology.

diseases.name: CDKL5 deficiency disorder
diseases.mechanism: CDKL5 loss of function; symptom control is distinct from causal restoration.
unresolved: No sourced causal CDKL5-restoring repurposed candidate in this pilot
Seizure endpoints do not establish developmental rescue

diseases.name: CACNA1A-related disorders
diseases.mechanism: Gain and loss of function both occur. A gene name alone cannot determine an intervention direction.
unresolved: Gain versus loss of function unresolved for a gene-only query

diseases.name: STXBP1-related disorder
diseases.mechanism: STXBP1 loss of function disrupts synaptic vesicle release.
unresolved: No sourced causal STXBP1-restoring repurposed candidate in this pilot

hero_journey.cluster_name: 15q11–q13 imprinting: shared assays, distinct therapeutic directions
hero_journey.family_explanation: Angelman syndrome can leave a key brain-cell protein, UBE3A, missing or reduced. Another community studies how nearby genes are switched on depending on which parent they came from. Their published cell-model work offers a starting point for sharing research methods, not medicines.

neighbor.name: Prader-Willi syndrome
neighbor.mechanism: Loss of paternal gene expression at the imprinted chromosome-15 region; different causal targets from Angelman.
neighbor.caveat: A complex, often multigene imprinting disorder. A research-asset neighbor, not an assertion of monogenic disease or transferable treatment.

asset.name: Published paired Angelman / Prader-Willi iPSC model approach
asset.availability: Protocol evidence verified; cell-line access, licensing and present researcher availability not verified.
asset.why_reusable: Both communities can discuss parent-of-origin expression and imprint maintenance readouts using the published paired model approach.
asset.researcher: Chamberlain et al. (publication team; current availability not verified)

counterexample.name: UBE3A dosage-gain neurodevelopmental phenotype
counterexample.explanation: A shared gene name is not a shared intervention direction. A restoration effect aligned with UBE3A deficiency should not be transferred to a dosage-gain context.
counterexample.distinction: Not included in the UBE3A-restoration therapeutic cluster. Broader Dup15q is multigenic; this is a direction counterexample, not a treatment model.
